title.narrative: Facilitating Business and Investment in Kenya-TRAC2

description.narrative: Kenya has a history of relatively strong economic growth, averaging 5-6% GDP growth pre-pandemic (though slowed by COVID-19). The economy recovered strongly in 2021, expanding at a rate of 7.5%, but pressure persisted in key areas, like tourism. In subsequent years, Kenyas real GDP increased from 4.8% in 2022 to an expected 5.4% in 2023. Economic growth has been fueled by a variety of sectors such as the agricultural, tourism and financial sectors making it a major role in the continents development trajectory. As a regional trade hub in East Africa, Kenya provides access to a wider market, offering significant potential for businesses. Kenya ranks fourth in Africa for business ease of doing business. With $3.86 billion in FDI projects registered in 2019, an all-time high, Kenya led the list of FDI in East Africa. However, economic growth in Kenya hasnt translated to lasting poverty reduction. National unemployment rates among the youth stand at about 39% with some counties having nearly half the youth population being unemployed. The Government, through its Bottom-Up Economic Transformation Approach (BETA), plans to create 1.2M jobs annually over the next five years. As such, the Government has prioritized improving business environment and promotion of investment towards private sector development and job creation. The goal of this PIP is to enhance the achievement of the SDGs by facilitating improvement in the business climate, export promotion and investment environment. UNDP Kenya will collaborate with the Government of Kenya and provide technical and financial assistance for the enhanced coordination and prioritization of business climate, enhancement of the investment and trade facilitation environment and formulation of the proposed Kenya’s International development assistance agency.
